title: Promotion attestation ledger and gated rollouts
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Objective: Build an auditable promotion attestation ledger and gated rollout workflow that enforces role-based approvals and attaches immutable evidence to every production model promotion (canary, A/B, shadow). The ledger must support multi-signer quorums, timeboxed sign-offs, and cryptographic attestations (HSM-backed signing) so we can meet enterprise compliance and provide forensic context for any rollback.

Scope:
- Ledger service: append-only promotion records with signer metadata, signed hashes of evidence bundles, and pointers to snapshots (metrics, evals, config).
- Approval policies: RBAC-driven policy engine mapping Okta groups to approval roles (owner, reviewer, approver) and configurable quorum by model risk label (low/medium/high).
- UI flows in Console: step-up authentication on high-risk promotions, explicit attestation modal, timebox expiration, forced re-approval after policy-changed.
- Runbook + automatic rollback: threshold-based auto-rollback hooks (latency/SLO/error-rate/quality regression) with prebuilt rollback playbooks and one-click human override.
- Evidence bundles: capture model artifact id, prompt set eval summary, canary traffic snapshot, per-route cost delta, and a signed metrics snapshot stored for N days (configurable retention).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Create promotion record via API or Console that contains signer list, policy id, and signed evidence hash.
2) Enforce multi-signature requirement for 'high' risk models before rollout can proceed to >10% traffic.
3) Console shows provenance timeline and provides download link for the signed evidence bundle.
4) Auto-rollback triggers when configured SLO breach persists for 5m with configurable cooldown; rollback event creates its own ledger entry and links to the original promotion.
5) Audit export available to SIEM (Splunk) in NDJSON with immutable IDs and signature verification metadata.

Design trade-offs and decisions:
- Chose an append-only ledger backed by object-store + signed manifest rather than a complex distributed database to simplify immutability guarantees and retention policies (trade-off: slightly slower lookup vs stronger forensic guarantees).
- Quorum policies will be policy-driven (declarative YAML) to avoid hardcoding org-specific roles; initial mapping integrates with Okta groups.
- Evidence bundles are stored encrypted with KMS and signed with an HSM key; this increases implementation complexity but is required for enterprise compliance.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Increased friction for model teams. Mitigation: Progressive enforcement (soft-mode for 60 days) and a developer preview with telemetry.
- Risk: KMS/HSM integration blocker. Mitigation: Engineering spike completed (ENG-39510), but cross-team coordination with Security required.

Open questions:
- Default retention period for evidence bundles (ops suggested 90d, compliance asked for 365d) -> decision pending legal review.
- Should low-risk models allow programmatic promotions without human signoff? PM leaning toward configurable per-customer policy.

Next steps / TODOs:
- Engineering: implement ledger API endpoints and policy evaluator (ENG-38902).
- Security: finish HSM key provisioning and KMS access policy (blocked on ticket ENG-39510).
- Console: add attestation UI modal and provenance timeline (design handoff 2025-02-25).
- SRE: wire auto-rollback events into existing alerting/ops playbooks and add synthetic checks.
